**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/03/10 (Fri) 17:13  
[EVENT] User is planning to plant seedlings in their backyard soon.  
[EVENT] User started marigold seeds that arrived on March 3rd, and they are already germinating.  
[PREFERENCE] User is excited to see their marigolds grow.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The ideal temperature for planting tomatoes outside is when the soil temperature reaches around 55°F (13°C) to 60°F (16°C) and the air temperature is around 65°F (18°C) to 70°F (21°C).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] For marigolds, the ideal temperature for planting outside is when the soil temperature reaches around 50°F (10°C) to 55°F (13°C).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should check the average last frost date for their area online before planting.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should harden off seedlings by gradually exposing them to outdoor conditions over 7-10 days.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should check specific instructions for each type of seedling or plant they are growing, as some may have different requirements.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To transplant seedlings, including marigolds, the assistant provided a step-by-step guide:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 1. Prepare the new pots (1-2 sizes larger, with drainage holes).  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 2. Water the seedlings the day before transplanting.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 3. Gather materials (new pots, transplanting tool, fresh potting soil).  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 4. Handle the roots with care when removing seedlings from pots.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 5. Inspect and trim any damaged or rotten roots.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 6. Add fresh potting soil to the new pot.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 7. Place the seedling in the new pot, ensuring the soil level is the same as in the original pot.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 8. Firm the soil around the roots.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 9. Water thoroughly after transplanting.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 10. Monitor and adjust care as needed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional tips to minimize shock include transplanting in the morning or late afternoon, avoiding extreme weather, keeping soil consistently moist, and providing support for seedlings.  
[PREFERENCE] User has been using a mix of peat moss, vermiculite, and perlite for potting soil.
